rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Source URL + type label — mandatory.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Source-verification block entry `willison-deviance` (line 186) reads '(no body URL — OODA findings workflow-composition-1a/3-confirmation)' with no clickable URL, yet the body (line 95) cites it as a direct claim: 'Willison has flagged the same pattern from a different angle, calling it normalization of deviance.' Per §1, no URL means the claim must be marked [SOURCE NEEDED]; it instead carries a `[checked:2026-05-25 result:OK due:2026-11-25]` stamp as if verified. Live-check today: Willison does have a real post using this exact phrase — 'The Normalization of Deviance in AI' (2025-12-10, simonwillison.net) — but it is about organizations becoming complacent toward AI security risk when no attack has yet occurred ('organizations confuse the absence of a successful attack with the presence of robust security'), not about composition fluency eroding review discipline. The body's framing ('the same pattern from a different angle') asserts Willison specifically addressed the composition-fluency claim, which he did not publish.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Add the real URL (simonwillison.net/2025/Dec/10/normalization-of-deviance/) and reframe the body sentence as the curriculum's own extension of Willison's coined term to a new domain, not as Willison having 'flagged the same pattern' — or drop the attribution to a bare cultural-vocab borrow of the term per §1's cultural-vocabulary carve-out.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: OODA paraphrase ≠ primary source.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Line 17: body states Klaassen's plugin ships 'the plugin's own four-stage naming' — Plan → Work → Assess → Compound. Live-fetch of github.com/EveryInc/compound-engineering-plugin today (2026-08-19) shows the README describes a six-stage cycle: 'The core loop is six steps: brainstorm the requirements, plan the implementation, work through the plan, simplify what you wrote, review the result, then compound the learning.' The plugin ships /ce-brainstorm and /ce-simplify-code alongside the four commands named in the body, and the README's own verb is 'review,' not 'assess' as the body claims. This is the exact drift shape the file's own maintainer note anticipates for the Klaassen entry (line 21, 'the plugin and the prose may simply have drifted apart') but the note frames drift as expected only between the plugin and Klaassen's separately-dated prose loop (line 21, dated 2026-05-29) — not as the plugin's own command set having grown since the 2026-05-25 check.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Re-verify the plugin's current stage-naming and command list against the live README; update the four-stage claim to six stages (or soften to 'the plugin names its stages differently from the numbers below, and both have moved since'), and correct 'Assess' to 'review' if that is still the plugin's own word.
